notes: Flight sticks, HOTAS, and gamepads can now be bound like keys. FleetComm's global input hook only ever saw keyboards and mice — a stick PTT that worked in QLink did nothing here because its buttons are a different kind of device entirely. Now: press any stick button once so Windows introduces the device to FleetComm (you'll see 'controller detected' in the COMM LOG), then click any KEY control — the PTT key, a per-net talk key, cycle keys — and press the stick button to bind it. Analog triggers count as pressed past 60% pull. Bindings survive replugging and USB port changes, and a stick button keys the net even while you're typing in chat (a stick can't type, so unlike a keyboard bind it doesn't wait for the text box). One honest caveat: this shipped tested against a simulated stick, not real hardware — if a real stick binds fine on the desktop but stops keying the net while the game has focus, say so immediately; that's the one behavior only a real cockpit can prove.
